provenance.source: PR #5707 feat(AxiosHeaders): add getSetCookie method to retrieve set-cookie headers values, squash-merged 2025-03-25 as 80ea756e7
provenance.note: Introduced by this PR: the accessor did not exist before, and it reads the object's own `set-cookie` property instead of going through the class's caseless `get()`. `AxiosHeaders.set()` stores a header it has not seen before under the name the caller passed (`self[key || _header]`), so `new AxiosHeaders({'Set-Cookie': ...})` and `set('Set-Cookie', ...)` both land on the mixed-case key while the accessor looks only at the lower-case one; the header is found only when it arrived already lower-cased (a parsed header string, or a Headers iteration). The later fix #6874 rewrites this one line to `this.get('set-cookie')` and adds no test, so the failing case is the caller-set header. Getter access, not the value, is what breaks: the values are present on the object under the original casing.

keywords: bypasses the caseless accessor and reads one fixed key
misses a header stored under its original casing
silently drops the values for a mixed-case header name
the header is not found when its name is not lower case
returns nothing for a header the caller already set
silently loses the values when the name is not lower case
bugs.note: the accessor indexes the object with one fixed lower-case key, but a header set under a mixed-case name is stored under that name, so the documented method returns an empty array; the fix routes the read through the caseless getter
